_note: The CONFIG VALIDATION grammar (D1) — the one new grammar R1 adds. A config entry may declare `pattern` (a regex the value must match), `validate` (a JSE expression returning true to pass or a string to fail with that message), and `message` (the author's words when `pattern` fails). Three planes consume this ONE vocabulary and must agree: config_schema.rb (the build gates prepare_config.rb + apply_core_config.rb), packages/kernel/src/config-validate.ts (the dashboard's live form AND the server's intake), and the Kotlin twin. A rule that passed at the form and failed at intake — or the reverse — is the class of bug this corpus exists to make impossible, because the user sees a green field and a rejected save.
_emptiness: AN EMPTY VALUE PASSES every rule here, deliberately, and `required` is the separate word that makes emptiness fail. This is not a convenience: it is the contract packages/dom/src/forms.ts already implements (`patternPasses` returns true on an empty value) and the Swift form contract it was written against. An optional field with a pattern would otherwise be impossible to leave blank.
_redos: A catastrophic-backtracking pattern is REFUSED rather than run — the value fails validation and the author is expected to rewrite the pattern. `reDoSProne` already exists as a tri-runtime twin (kernel/src/jse/regex.ts, Jse.kt, Stack.swift) and is REUSED here rather than reimplemented; these cases pin that the config plane calls it, not that it works.

limits._why: The same ceiling forms.ts applies. A pattern longer than this is refused unread: a synchronous regex has no timeout on a single-threaded event loop.

cases.name: no-rules-declared-passes-anything
cases._why: The overwhelmingly common entry declares no validation at all and must stay free.

cases.name: message-overrides-the-default-when-pattern-fails
cases._why: The author's words are the whole point of `message`: 'Invalid format' tells a user nothing about a bundle id.

entry.message: Use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens

expect.message: Use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens

cases.name: an-empty-value-passes-a-pattern
cases._why: The emptiness contract. Pair with `required` when blank must fail.

cases.name: validate-returning-a-STRING-fails-with-that-string
cases._why: The reason a `validate` expression beats a pattern: it can say WHY, computed from the value.

entry.validate: value.length > 3 ? true : 'Needs at least 4 characters, got ' + value.length

cases.name: an-explicit-message-does-NOT-override-a-validate-string
cases._why: Precedence, stated once: a computed reason is more specific than a static one, so it wins. `message` is the fallback, not an override.

cases.name: pattern-runs-before-validate
cases._why: Deterministic order, so the message a user sees does not depend on which rule the implementation happened to check first.

cases.name: a-redos-prone-pattern-is-refused
cases._why: Star height 2. Refused unread rather than executed: a synchronous regex has no timeout, so running it is how one hostile config entry freezes an SSR process.

cases.name: an-invalid-regex-fails-closed-rather-than-throwing
cases._why: A malformed pattern is an authoring bug; it must surface as a failed field, never as an exception that takes down the form or the request.

cases.name: validate-sees-the-value-and-nothing-else
cases._why: The seam is one name. A validate expression is authored config, evaluated on the server at intake as well as in the browser, so it reaches `value` and no host object — JSE has no name for anything else by construction.

cases.name: a-non-string-value-validates-against-its-string-form
cases._why: Config entries are typed (number, boolean, list), and a pattern is a string rule. Coercing once here beats each plane inventing its own coercion.

cases.name: a-list-value-validates-every-member
cases._why: A list entry with a pattern means every entry must match; one bad member fails the field.
